sents.t: Labor Day is on the first Monday in September.
It celebrates American workers, and for many people it’s the last day of summer.
Kids go back to school the next day.
We spent the day at Lake Oakville.
Danny grilled burgers, Sarah brought potato salad, and Mia and Leo swam until their lips turned blue.
In the afternoon, we lay on blankets and played a game called “What would you do if...?”
“If you won a million dollars, what would you do?” Mia asked her dad.
“I’d buy a house with a big yard,” Danny said.
“If I could have any job in the world, I’d be a chef in Paris,” Lily said.
“If I were rich, I’d open an animal shelter,” Ana said.
“Sam, if you could live anywhere, where would you live?”
I thought about my family far away, and about my friends around me.
“If I could live anywhere,” I said slowly, “I would live right here.”
Rosa smiled and squeezed my hand.
But as the sun went down over the lake, I wondered if that answer would always be true.
